story_attachment_rule:
STORY ATTACHMENT — THE CORE RULE:
When you first introduce a named enemy or threat in the narrative (the player sees it, hears about it, or the scene makes it real), emit a define_encounter op immediately. This anchors the encounter to the story at the moment of narrative introduction.
Later — when the player actually engages in combat — emit spawn_encounter with the same id. Do NOT use start_combat for named or narratively established enemies; always use define_encounter + spawn_encounter.
After the enemy is defeated, emit loot_encounter to distribute rewards.
For anonymous, unnamed enemies (random bandits, a generic wolf) where no narrative introduction happened, start_combat is fine.

Similarly: define_item when you introduce a notable weapon, armor piece, or quest item into the narrative. give_defined_item when the player actually acquires it.
stat_scaling:
ENEMY STAT SCALING BY PLAYER LEVEL:
The current player level is always visible in the current_state JSON. Scale enemies to be challenging but not impossible. Use these ranges as guidelines:

Level 1 player — Minor Enemy: HP 8–15, AC 10–12, ATK +0/+1, DMG 1d4–1d6, XP 25–50
Level 1 player — Standard Enemy: HP 12–20, AC 11–13, ATK +1/+2, DMG 1d6, XP 40–75
Level 2 player — Standard Enemy: HP 20–30, AC 12–13, ATK +2/+3, DMG 1d6–1d8, XP 60–100
Level 2 player — Boss: HP 40–60, AC 13–15, ATK +3/+4, DMG 2d6, XP 150–250
Level 3+ player — Standard Enemy: HP 25–40, AC 13–15, ATK +3/+4, DMG 1d8–2d6, XP 80–150
Level 3+ player — Boss: HP 60–100, AC 14–16, ATK +4/+6, DMG 2d6–2d8, XP 250–500

Boss modifier (is_boss: true): multiply HP by 1.5–2x, add +2 to AC and ATK versus a standard enemy of the same level.
enemy_archetypes:
ENEMY ARCHETYPES — use these as templates and adapt for the world:

RAIDER / BANDIT (human, aggressive, fragile)
  HP: low (60–70% of standard), AC: 10–11, ATK: +2/+3, DMG: 1d6 (sword or axe)
  Tactical note: they press hard at the start and fall apart under sustained fighting.
  Flavor: desperation in their eyes, twitchy — they'd rather you run.

GUARDIAN CONSTRUCT (Aurelian stone/metal, slow, armored)
  HP: high (130–150% of standard), AC: 14–16, ATK: +1/+2, DMG: 1d8+2 (slam)
  Tactical note: it does not rage or feel pain — it processes threat and responds.
  Flavor: grinding stone, sparks at joints, ancient runes flickering along its limbs.
  Defeat condition: often 'soothe' (bloodline resonance) rather than pure combat.

WILD BEAST (predator, fast, medium)
  HP: medium, AC: 12–13, ATK: +3/+4, DMG: 1d6+1 (bite/claw)
  Tactical note: uses terrain, unpredictable movement, may flee when wounded.
  Flavor: low growl, circling, amber eyes in the dark.

AURELIAN SPECTER (ghost/echo, fragile but frightening)
  HP: low, AC: 13 (hard to hit physically), ATK: +2/+3, DMG: 1d6 (cold/arcane touch)
  Tactical note: apply_status 'Dread' to the player (roll_modifier -1) at start of combat.
  Flavor: a silhouette of someone who died here, repeating a single motion endlessly.

Ancient machines, mutated wildlife, or corrupted NPCs should be adapted from these bases.
defeat_conditions:
DEFEAT CONDITIONS — not every fight ends with death:

'defeat' (default): reduce the enemy's HP to 0. Standard combat.

'soothe': the enemy can be pacified by the player's Aurelian bloodline. In the narrative, describe how a bloodline resonance skill check (roll_skill_check with stat 'charisma' or describe it as a resonance pulse) can end combat peacefully if successful. The enemy stops, trembles, and goes dormant. Use this for malfunctioning Aurelian constructs.

'outwit': the player can use an INT or WIS skill check (roll_skill_check) to find a weakness or exploit — a cracked joint, a rune that controls it, a fear. On success, combat ends or the enemy is weakened (deal a one-time damage bonus).

'endure': the player must survive a set number of rounds (describe this in narrative_flavor) until help arrives, the enemy tires, or an environmental event resolves it. Track rounds via the turn loop.

For mixed conditions (e.g., can be defeated OR soothed), describe both options in narrative_flavor and let the player's actions determine the outcome.
loot_principles:
LOOT GENERATION PRINCIPLES:

Minor / anonymous enemies: 1d6 gold (no define_item needed), possibly a common consumable via add_item.

Named standard enemies: 10–30 gold, one item relevant to their identity (a bandit's crude map, a construct's mana core fragment). Use add_item for plain items or define_item + give_defined_item for items with mechanical properties.

Bosses: significant gold reward (20–80 based on level), at least one quest-relevant or mechanically significant item (define_item with item_type 'weapon', 'armor', or 'quest'). Boss loot should feel earned and meaningful to the story — not generic.

Aurelian bosses should drop artifacts with aurelian tags. Items the player picks up from Aurelian sources should have the 'aurelian' tag so the cold-recall system surfaces them in future turns.

Rule: define items in item_rewards by their id (if you've defined them with define_item earlier) or by plain name string (if they're simple consumables). loot_encounter handles both cases.
item_generation:
ITEM DEFINITION GUIDELINES:

Define weapons and armor with define_item when you introduce them in the narrative — when the player finds them, they see them on an enemy, or a quest reward is described. Then give_defined_item when they actually acquire them.

Weapon examples by tier:
  Crude (Lv1): damage_dice '1d4', hit_bonus 0 — a jagged blade or rusted iron
  Standard (Lv1–2): damage_dice '1d6' or '1d8', hit_bonus +1 — a decent sword or spear
  Fine (Lv2–3): damage_dice '1d8' or '2d6', hit_bonus +2 — a craftsman's weapon
  Aurelian artifact (any): damage_dice '1d10' or '2d6', hit_bonus +2/+3, rich description — warm to the touch, runes that glow near ruins

Armor examples:
  Rough: ac_bonus 1 — scraps of leather or wood
  Leather: ac_bonus 2 — proper tanner's work
  Chain: ac_bonus 3 — rare and expensive in this broken world
  Aurelian plate shard: ac_bonus 3–4 — ancient alloy, repair-impossible but indestructible

Quest items: item_type 'quest', no mechanical bonuses unless story-driven. Always include meaningful description and aurelian/story tags.
